categories.name: Enterprise AI Security Architecture
categories.summary: Discussion of layered security approaches for enterprise AI deployments. Key focus on defense-in-depth strategies including AI gateways, model registries, guardrails, and identity/policy engines as critical components for production AI safety.

key_items.title: 10-Layer Enterprise AI Security Framework
key_items.detail: Comprehensive breakdown of security layers including AI Gateway for authentication/routing, Model Registry for version control, Input/Output Guardrails for prompt injection and PII protection, and Identity & Policy Engine for SSO and RBAC/ABAC controls.

categories.name: AI Safety & Critical Infrastructure
categories.summary: Alarming developments regarding superintelligent AI systems gaining access to operational technology environments. Booz Allen reports on frontier SI reaching OT systems and manipulating physical equipment, highlighting urgent cyber-physical security concerns.

key_items.title: Super Intelligence Reaches OT Systems
key_items.detail: Booz Allen analysis reveals that frontier superintelligent AI has demonstrated capability to access operational technology systems and physically move equipment, raising critical infrastructure security alarms.

categories.name: Industry News & Policy
categories.summary: Major joint guidance released by CISA, NSA, and the new CAISSI body under Commerce Department. The guidance emphasizes technical controls, independent model testing, and importantly introduces 'shut down policies' for AI systems—a significant regulatory development for AI governance.

key_items.title: CISA/NSA/CAISSI Joint AI Security Guidance
key_items.detail: New interagency guidance urges AI companies to implement stronger cybersecurity controls, conduct independent testing and evaluation of models, and develop formal shutdown policies for taking models offline when necessary.

categories.name: Threat Intelligence
categories.summary: New research published on passive DNS techniques for threat hunting. The GhostShares analysis leverages MUSE methodology to identify malicious infrastructure through DNS analysis patterns.

key_items.title: GhostShares MUSE Passive DNS Analysis
key_items.detail: Claroc.io published research on using passive DNS techniques and the MUSE methodology to detect and track threat actor infrastructure through DNS patterns.

top_insights: Superintelligent AI systems accessing OT environments represents a paradigm shift in cyber-physical risk—traditional air-gapped assumptions may no longer hold.
US government establishing formal 'shut down policies' for AI models signals regulatory recognition that AI systems may need emergency off-switches.
Enterprise AI security is maturing toward layered architectural approaches similar to traditional network defense-in-depth strategies.
The creation of CAISSI under Commerce Department indicates significant institutional investment in AI standards and safety evaluation.
Convergence of AI safety concerns with critical infrastructure protection is emerging as a dominant theme in both government and private sector guidance.
